findings.title: Login-cache invalidation decision uses org-aware isEnabled(), which can leave a stale login IDP list
findings.body:
In `update()`, `idpById` comes from `getById()`, which returns the `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel` wrapper. Its `isEnabled()` returns false whenever the linked organization is disabled. `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` feeds this into `getLoginPredicate()`. The cached ID set, however, is built by `idpDelegate.getForLogin`, which filters on raw DB fields (enabled, hideOnLogin, linkOnly, BROKER_PUBLIC) and ignores organization enablement.

Repro: an IDP linked to org A is public, enabled and shown, so it is in the cached ORG_ONLY/ALL lists. Org A is then disabled. An admin sets `hideOnLogin=true`, `linkOnly=true` or removes `BROKER_PUBLIC`. The original evaluates as not-login (wrapper reports disabled) and the updated model is also not-login, so the first early return fires and nothing is invalidated. The cached list still holds the IDP's id.

Once org A is re-enabled, `getForLogin` returns the IDP from cache. `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` only re-checks `isEnabled()`, not hideOnLogin, linkOnly or public. A hidden, link-only or non-public broker is therefore displayed on the login page until something else invalidates the key.

Fix: base the original-state check on the raw stored model (e.g. `idpDelegate.getById`), or always invalidate when any `LoginFilter` field, `BROKER_PUBLIC` or the org link changes.

findings.title: Single per-mode login cache entry grows with every organization and is rebuilt on each new org lookup
findings.body:
All `getForLogin` results for a fetch mode share one cache key (`<realm>.idp.login.<mode>`), with the organizationId only used as a sub-key inside `IdentityProviderListQuery`. The first lookup for each new organization calls `cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey)`, which bumps the revision. It then re-adds a new query object that copies every previously cached org result set.

For `FetchMode.ALL`, each per-org set also duplicates all realm-level login IDPs. In realms with many organizations, the entry grows roughly as O(orgs × IDPs). Login traffic for different orgs keeps invalidating and rewriting the same entry, and concurrent requests race on the revision, so their caching attempts are discarded. Consider keying the cache by mode and organizationId instead.

findings.title: Test cleanup removes literal "alias" instead of the created IDPs
findings.body: `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` binds the cleanup to an IDP whose alias is the string "alias", not to `"idp-alias-" + i`. The same mistake appears again at line 425 for `idp-alias-20`. None of the IDPs created by `testCacheIDPForLogin` are cleaned up. Instead, cleanup issues repeated removals of a non-existent IDP, which may fail with 404 or be silently swallowed. Use the actual alias, e.g. `final String alias = "idp-alias-" + i; ... get(alias)::remove`.
